thought.text: Found it — the token endpoint is `http://localhost/service/token`. Let me retry the cleanup with a proper delete-scoped token.

reasoning_content: The registry's token endpoint is `http://localhost/service/token`, not `/c/token`. The core API's WWW-Authenticate uses Basic for unauthenticated, but works with bearer. My previous DELETE attempts to the core API using `/c/token`-derived tokens returned 401 because… no, wait, earlier the GET using a `/c/token`-derived token on the same endpoint returned 405 (method not allowed, so authentication was OK). And the DELETE returned 401 "unauthorized". Hmm, but the token from `/c/token` was valid for GET (the artifacts list worked). Actually, the earlier 405 was GET against the tags endpoint, which is not implemented. The DELETE 401 with a valid token might have been because the token didn't have the `delete` scope. Harbor's UI token from /c/token may only have system scopes… Actually, the core API authorizes via its own middleware. Let's use the correct endpoint `http://localhost/service/token` with delete scope.

action.command:
RESP=$(curl -s 'http://localhost/service/token?service=harbor-registry&scope=repository:library/alpine:pull,delete&grant_type=password&username=admin&password=Harbor12345')
TTOK=$(echo "$RESP" | sed -n 's/.*"access_token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
echo "token len=${#TTOK}"
DIGEST='sha256:7cefa58bd70cbf86bb0ef44b9c27a9c6a633763977ea40868d1bfe9278967b25'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'DELETE validation-test tag -> HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TTOK" "http://localhost/api/v2.0/projects/library/repositories/alpine/artifacts/${DIGEST}/tags/validation-test"
sleep 2
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TTOK" http://localhost/v2/library/alpine/tags/list; echo
